page: OVHcloud h100-760 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server powered by an AMD EPYC 9354 processor with 60 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. The system features 760.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 12.67 GB of memory per core. For acceleration, it integrates two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs with a combined 160 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 4040 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, with stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 10%. The server excels in LLM inference, achieving top-tier speeds for prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large 70B models. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth ranks in the top 10%, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths perform in the middle 50%. Redis SET operations also reach top-tier throughput.

Given the integration of dual NVIDIA H100 GPUs and a high-density memory configuration, this server represents a high-resource hardware class designed for intensive parallel computing. The qualitative cost profile reflects its specialized hardware density, trading general-purpose budget efficiency for extreme compute and acceleration capabilities. It is highly suited for large language model inference, deep learning training, ray tracing, high-performance database operations, and complex scientific simulations.
description: The OVHcloud h100-760 is a high-performance GPU-accelerated server designed for intensive computational workloads. It features an AMD EPYC 9354 processor with 60 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 760.0 GB of RAM. The server is equipped with two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs providing a total of 160 GB of VRAM, alongside a 4040 GB NVMe SSD and a 16 Gbps network interface. Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU tasks, Redis operations, and LLM inference across small, medium, and large models. While large-block memory bandwidth operates at average levels, the system's massive parallel processing capabilities make it highly effective for deep learning, large-scale database operations, and complex simulation workloads.
